speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: asked the Minister for Manpower with an increasing number of Singaporeans in PMET jobs, whether CPF LIFE will be updated to allow the option for more voluntary savings under the CPF scheme to provide for retirement payouts closer to PMETs' pre-retirement income.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This Enhanced Retirement Sum is revised annually, together with the Basic and Full Retirement Sums.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I believe there was just an article over the weekend in The Straits Times about how this lady who has, I think, something like $1.6 million in her CPF and has opted to defer the payout of her retirement income up to age 70.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Perhaps Ms Foo Mee Har can take heart in the fact that there are Singaporeans who have accumulated those surpluses.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Apart from the CPF system, Singaporeans can also save more during their working years, by making voluntary contributions to the Supplementary Retirement Scheme (SRS).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The savings in the SRS plus any investment gains, can be used to purchase private annuity plans, which can further supplement CPF LIFE payouts.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: In fact, I am a big fan of the CPF scheme.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Actually, my question is very specifically targeted at CPF LIFE.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: My supplementary question for the Minister is: as more Singaporeans are realising the attractiveness of this specific scheme, CPF LIFE, which gives you a lifetime income, especially in the current challenging investment environment, and we are seeing more seniors falling victim to investment scams in their pursuit of higher returns on their hard-earned savings in order to sustain their post-pandemic lifestyle.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: And I think the House would agree that, at the current cost of living, $2,000 is quite basic and this is at an enhanced level.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Why not offer Singaporeans the option to save more under CPF LIFE in order to receive up to, say, the current CPF monthly contributions, capped at, say, $6,000 a month or, minimally, at around the prevailing median income of around $4,500 now?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We are also heartened that more members are topping up their CPF accounts and for their trust in the CPF system as well as the acknowledgement of the benefits that CPF and CPF LIFE can offer.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: CPF interest rates are pegged to risk-free market instruments of comparable duration.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: CPF members do not bear any investment risks to enjoy these favourable interest rates.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It is guaranteed by the Government and any investment risk is absorbed by the Government's balance sheet.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Without a limit that is set as a cap, higher-income members could channel large savings into their Retirement Account and CPF LIFE.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Collectively, the CPF Board and the Ministry of Manpower are reviewing over the longer run and we take cognisance of the Member's exhortation and suggestion in terms of finding other types of instruments to allow our CPF members to be able to place their savings with.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I believe that, in time to come, we should be able to share when the plan is ready.
